entries.description: Read-only REST discovery over the APIs.io catalog of API providers, their APIs, and the artifacts each publishes. The same contract generates the MCP server, so the two never drift. Catalog reads are free and keyless.
representativeQueries: search API providers and their APIs over REST
list the machine-readable artifacts a provider publishes
look up an API rating and its rubric

entries.description: Learn how to read the apis.io API catalog — the v1 REST API, the MCP server, and the markdown mirror of every page — so other skills can find APIs without scraping HTML. Use this first when the user mentions apis.io or asks to discover APIs across a catalog.
representativeQueries: how do I read the apis.io catalog
what interfaces does apis.io expose

entries.description: Turn a domain, URL, company name, or GitHub org into an apis.io provider slug, with its quality band and composite score. Use first whenever the user names a company rather than a catalog slug — which is almost always.
representativeQueries: turn a company name into a catalog slug
which provider is this domain

entries.description: Search the apis.io catalog for APIs, providers, and tags by keyword, capability, tag, or provider. Use when the user asks what APIs exist for something, which providers offer a capability, or wants to filter the catalog.
representativeQueries: search for APIs by keyword
find APIs in an industry

entries.description: Fetch and parse the OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL, or Postman description for an API in the apis.io catalog, given its aid or its apis.io URL. Use to inspect operations, summarize endpoints, or generate code from a real spec.
representativeQueries: get the OpenAPI for this provider
download an API specification

entries.description: Find the right API for a task — search the apis.io catalog, inspect the strongest candidates, and recommend one with its spec and links. Use when the user asks what API to use for something, or whether an API exists for a job.
representativeQueries: find an API that can do this task
which API handles payments

entries.description: Onboard an API provider end-to-end — pull its signup, authentication, base URLs and OpenAPI from the apis.io catalog and produce concrete, runnable first-integration steps. Use when a provider is chosen and the user wants to actually wire it up.
representativeQueries: how do I onboard with this API
what does integration take

entries.description: Find providers in the apis.io catalog that publish an MCP server, with the endpoint and install method, so you can plug real tools into an agent. Use when the user wants agent-ready tools rather than raw REST.
representativeQueries: which providers run an MCP server
find MCP servers for a task

entries.description: Search the apis.io catalog for Agent Skills published by API providers — packaged SKILL.md files you can adopt directly. Use when the user wants ready-made skills for a vendor or capability rather than writing integration code.
representativeQueries: which providers publish agent skills
find agent skills for a vendor

entries.description: Search the apis.io catalog for any artifact type beyond OpenAPI — Arazzo workflows, Spectral rules, pricing plans, FinOps, rate limits, GraphQL, Postman collections, JSON Schemas, examples, and more. Use when the user wants governance, commercial, or workflow artifacts rather than an API contract.
representativeQueries: find providers publishing AsyncAPI
who publishes Arazzo workflows

entries.description: Check whether an API provider is ready for autonomous AI agents — machine-readable contracts, MCP servers, agent skills, llms.txt, agent-native access controls, and the operational signals an agent needs. Use when asked if an API is agent-ready, or to compare providers on agent readiness.
representativeQueries: is this provider ready for agents
scan a domain for agent readiness

entries.description: Read a provider's apis.io quality score and the Kin Score rubric, then turn it into a ranked, do-this-next punch list of what to publish to move up a band. Use when someone wants to know how their own API rates and how to improve it.
representativeQueries: what is my API rated
how do I raise my score

entries.description: Check where an apis.io provider record's evidence came from — which artifacts the provider published first-party versus which apis.io derived — before citing a score or an artifact as fact. Use when accuracy matters, or when a provider disputes their rating.
representativeQueries: where did this catalog claim come from
show the evidence for this rating

entries.description: Turn one capability into a scored, compared vendor shortlist from the apis.io catalog, with a clear recommendation. Use for a buy decision on a single capability. Pro tier.
representativeQueries: shortlist vendors for this capability
which API vendor should we pick

entries.description: Design a capability stack from the apis.io catalog — the best-rated provider per capability — and export it as an adoptable APIs.json. Use when the user needs several APIs at once, not one. Pro tier.
representativeQueries: design an API stack for this product
which APIs do I need for this build

entries.description: Inventory, score, and gap a set of API providers from the apis.io catalog — what they publish, how they rate, and what they are missing. Use to assess a vendor portfolio. Pro tier.
representativeQueries: audit the APIs our company depends on
review our API estate

entries.description: Benchmark one API provider against its closest peers facet by facet — score, artifact coverage, and where it leads or trails. Use for competitive positioning or to justify an API investment. Pro tier, with a free fallback.
representativeQueries: how do we compare to our competitors
benchmark our API against peers

entries.description: Explore any slice of the API market as a scored cohort — an industry, topic area, region, or tag — with its members, their Kin Scores and agent readiness. Use to size a market, find the leaders in a category, or research a sector.
representativeQueries: explore a group of similar providers
what does this industry publish

entries.description: Read the demand side of the API market — what technologies a company is investing in, where it is thin, and which catalog providers are already in its stack. Use for account research, sales targeting, or to find where demand outruns supply.
representativeQueries: is this company ready for agent traffic
assess a company API surface

entries.description: Set up ongoing monitoring of the apis.io catalog using saved searches and lists — track a vendor set, get only what is new since last check, and watch for rating movement. Use for recurring vendor monitoring rather than one-off queries. Pro tier, with a free fallback.

watch these APIs for updates

entries.description: Monitor the apis.io catalog for providers added or updated and for rating movement, across a chosen set or the whole network. Use for ongoing vendor monitoring. Pro tier.

track deprecations across my dependencies
